research_question: RQ9: Which components degrade first under semantic/sensory shifts?
data_source: BDD100K val set — 500 images, real GroundingDINO inference

ECE.interpretation: ECE decreased 19.3% (from 0.150 to 0.121). This is a selection bias artifact: shift suppressed 62.1% of detections, leaving only high-confidence surviving detections. ECE improvement is NOT a real calibration gain.

conclusion: mAP drops 24.0% under maximum shift, confirming detection quality collapse. AURC increases 20.3%, confirming uncertainty ranking degrades under shift. Risk@80% coverage increases by 0.128 absolute. ECE decreased 19.3% (from 0.150 to 0.121). This is a selection bias artifact: shift suppressed 62.1% of detections, leaving only high-confidence surviving detections. ECE improvement is NOT a real calibration gain. The dominant post-hoc reliability limit is ranking degradation (AURC), not miscalibration of surviving detections.
